crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Biodiversity Officer (15298) Requisition ID 15298 - Posted - Job Function (2) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List 12-month, fixed term parental leave back fill opportunity based at Kew Play a role in protecting and enhancing Boroondara’s unique biodiversity for future generations $87,101 - $100,905 plus super and monthly RDO The Role We are seeking an enthusiastic and community-focused Biodiversity Officer to join our Urban Biodiversity and Revegetation team for 12 months, backfilling a parental leave role. Reporting to the Coordinator Urban Biodiversity and Revegetation, you will support the delivery of biodiversity initiatives that help protect, enhance and celebrate Boroondara's natural habitat. You will play an important role in engaging our community and supporting actions that contribute to positive environmental outcomes. The successful candidate must be available to commence in the role prior to Christmas 2026. Key Responsibilities You will plan and deliver biodiversity projects and initiatives that support Council's biodiversity objectives and action plans. You will help develop innovative programs and activities that encourage community participation and understanding of local biodiversity. You will coordinate and deliver workshops, presentations, citizen science activities and community events designed to educate and engage residents of all ages whilst also promoting biodiversity programs and events. About You You are passionate about biodiversity, environmental sustainability and community engagement. You enjoy building relationships and can communicate effectively with a wide range of stakeholders, from community volunteers and residents to professional colleagues and external agencies. You will bring experience delivering projects, events or programs, together with strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities. You will hold a qualification in Environmental Management, Environmental Science, Sustainability, Conservation Management or a related discipline, or possess equivalent relevant experience in environmental sustainability, biodiversity or community engagement. About Boroondara The City of Boroondara is home to some of Melbourne's most treasured parks, waterways and natural environments. We are committed to creating a healthy, connected and sustainable community and place our customers at the centre of everything we do. Our people are passionate about delivering meaningful outcomes for our community while living our values of Innovation, Integrity, Respect, Ownership, Collaboration and Customer Focus. Why Join Us This is an exciting opportunity to contribute directly to the protection and enhancement of biodiversity across one of Melbourne's most beautiful municipalities. You will work with passionate professionals, collaborate with dedicated community volunteers and help deliver initiatives that make a lasting environmental impact. At Boroondara, we offer a supportive and inclusive workplace, flexible working arrangements, professional development opportunities and a culture that encourages collaboration, innovation and continuous improvement. For more information, please refer to the attached Position Description. Employment Requirements Applicants must hold valid working rights in Australia, and those progressing through the selection process will need to complete a National Police Record Check, a Working with Children Check and relevant pre-employment medical assessments. How to Apply Please submit your application online via the 'Apply' button by 11.59pm, Sunday 15 November 2026. All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. For a confidential discussion about this position please contact Amy Shaw , Coordinator Urban Biodiversity and Revegetation on 0419 745 256 during business hours or amy.shaw@boroondara.vic.gov.au . We are seeking skilled and experienced professional care workers who love supporting people to live independently in the community. We currently provide services in Mount Alexander Shire and Central Goldfields Shire. This is your opportunity to bring your passion and skills to be part of a professional and dedicated team providing high quality in-home support to frail older people and people with disabilities in our community. The role provides tailored services to help clients live healthy, independent and active lives through assistance with daily tasks and activities. Direct Care Worker Traineeship Opportunities: If you don’t already have a certificate III in Individual Support, you can also apply here for a Trainee Direct Care Worker position, to earn and learn on the job. Minimum Qualifications and Experience You must have, or be willing to obtain: Current Police Check Current Working with Children Check Triple vaccinated for COVID (2 doses plus a booster). Current Drivers license and roadworthy, registered and comprehensively insured vehicle for work travel Applicants must be able to work weekends. First Aid and CPR certificate will be gained though training and applied to the role as required If you have any queries or would like to discuss the role, the key contacts are: Sarah Newstead In Home Support Coordinator – East (03) 5471 1845 Talia Jenkin In Home Support Coordinator – West (03) 5471 1728 To apply for a Direct Care Worker or Direct Care Worker Trainee position, please provide a cover letter (no more than 2 pages) outlining why you are interested and the best candidate for this role, and your current resume. Additional information Mount Alexander Shire Council is committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to child safety with zero tolerance for child abuse. We value a diverse workforce and encourage applicants from all cultures, sexual orientations, gender identities and backgrounds. Applicants can expect that the recruitment process will include interviewing, reference checks and criminal history checks. Some positions will also be required to provide a Working with Children Check, and medical assessments including drug and alcohol testing may be undertaken. For more information on the recruitment process, please download the Candidate information document from our website.
